# ISA Reference

This page is generated from the assembler opcode table and checked against the Python reference model metadata.

## Encoding

Each instruction is one byte: bits `[7:4]` hold the opcode and bits `[3:0]` hold the operand nibble.
Instruction memory and data memory each contain 16 entries, so address operands are 4-bit values.

## Valid Opcodes

| Opcode | Mnemonic | Operand | Encoding | Behavior | Flags | PC effect | Memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x0` | `NOP` | `none` | `0x00` (`operand` ignored by RTL for this opcode) | No operation. | unchanged | PC + 1 | none |
| `0x1` | `LDI` | `imm4` | `0x1n`, where `n` is `imm4` | Load zero-extended 4-bit immediate into ACC. | Z set from ACC; N=0, C=0, V=0 | PC + 1 | none |
| `0x2` | `ADD` | `addr4` | `0x2n`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = ACC + DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N, C, V updated | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0x3` | `SUB` | `addr4` | `0x3n`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = ACC - DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N, C, V updated | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0x4` | `STA` | `addr4` | `0x4n`, where `n` is `addr4` | DMEM[addr4] = ACC. | unchanged | PC + 1 | write DMEM[addr4] |
| `0x5` | `LDA` | `addr4` | `0x5n`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N updated; C=0, V=0 | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0x6` | `JMP` | `addr4` | `0x6n`, where `n` is `addr4` | Unconditional branch. | unchanged | PC = addr4 | none |
| `0x7` | `JZ` | `addr4` | `0x7n`, where `n` is `addr4` | Branch when ZERO is set. | unchanged | PC = addr4 if ZERO else PC + 1 | none |
| `0x8` | `HLT` | `none` | `0x80` (`operand` ignored by RTL for this opcode) | Halt execution. | unchanged | PC holds | none |
| `0x9` | `AND` | `addr4` | `0x9n`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = ACC & DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N updated; C=0, V=0 | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0xA` | `OR` | `addr4` | `0xAn`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = ACC \| DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N updated; C=0, V=0 | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0xB` | `XOR` | `addr4` | `0xBn`, where `n` is `addr4` | ACC = ACC ^ DMEM[addr4]. | Z, N updated; C=0, V=0 | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |
| `0xC` | `SHL` | `none` | `0xC0` (`operand` ignored by RTL for this opcode) | ACC = ACC << 1. | Z, N, C, V updated | PC + 1 | none |
| `0xD` | `SHR` | `none` | `0xD0` (`operand` ignored by RTL for this opcode) | ACC = ACC >> 1. | Z, N, C updated; V=0 | PC + 1 | none |
| `0xE` | `CMP` | `addr4` | `0xEn`, where `n` is `addr4` | Update flags from ACC - DMEM[addr4]; ACC is unchanged. | Z, N, C, V updated | PC + 1 | read DMEM[addr4] |

## Illegal Opcode

`0xF*` is intentionally left illegal. The RTL and Python reference model both trap it by setting `HALTED=1` and holding `PC`.

## Consistency Checks

Run the generated-doc check with:

```bash
bash scripts/check-python-model.sh
```

Regenerate this page after intentional ISA edits with:

```bash
bash scripts/generate-isa-docs.sh
```
